_comment: Partial upper coverage (schema_version 2) -- the counterexample of review round 2,
defect 3: 'the upper storey only covers part of the lower room'.  The ground-floor
hall (8 x 6 m) is covered by the first-storey landing over its southern half only
(y in [0, 3]); over the northern half (y in [3, 6]) the hall keeps its OWN ceiling
slab.  The old _ceiling_is_upper_slab() dropped the whole room's ceiling as soon as
any overlap existed, so the northern half ended up open to the sky.
Two slab openings of floor f1 are declared: the stairwell the straight stair rises
through (1.9..6.1 x 0.9..2.1) and a 1 x 1 m void over the COVERED half (6.5..7.5 x
0.5..1.5) -- a double-height space, i.e. an explicit void declared by slab_opening.
The ground floor keeps the legacy 0.05 m slab while f1 is 0.15 m thick, so the two
bodies can be told apart by rays: in the uncovered half the hall's own ceiling
spans 2.70..2.75 m, in the covered half the f1 slab spans 2.70..2.85 m.
Rays in the three regions: covered -> the f1 slab bottom at 2.70 m (top 2.85 m);
uncovered -> the hall's own ceiling bottom at 2.70 m (top 2.75 m) -- with the old
room-wide skip this ray hit NOTHING within 20 m; void -> no body at all around
2.70 m, the first upward hit is the landing roof at 5.55 m.
